subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this RFC as a core control-plane/runtime architecture, narrow it to subagent/ACP execution placement only, or defer it as too heavy for the current roadmap?
rationale: The repository has partial runtime policy and ACP/subagent control-plane seams, but the full proposal changes process boundaries, secret isolation, config shape, session ownership, channel delivery, and deployment operations.

options.title: Keep RFC as core architecture track
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate a staged core design for runtime protocol, security, session ownership, and compatible embedded/local-split/distributed modes.

options.title: Narrow to subagent placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the active scope and leave the full Gateway/runtime split out for now.

options.title: Defer as heavy orchestration
options.body: Freeze or close this direction until security, stability, setup, and harness priorities create enough need for a core orchestration layer.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC as core architecture track
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate a staged core design for runtime protocol, security, session ownership, and compatible embedded/local-split/distributed modes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP spawn work is the strongest current-main history signal for the runtime/control-plane decision surface.
